topic: Literature, Science & Culture of Ancient India

items.title: Languages, Scripts and Classical Languages
items.body:
Indian languages fall into four families: **Indo-Aryan** (~74%, from Sanskrit → Prakrit/Pali → modern Hindi, Bengali, Marathi, Urdu…), **Dravidian** (~25%, Tamil/Telugu/Kannada/Malayalam), **Sino-Tibetan** (Himalayan/NE, e.g. Manipuri) and **Austric/Austro-Asiatic** (Santhali, Khasi, Nicobarese). Tamil is the oldest Dravidian language; Telugu is the largest.

Ancient **scripts**: Brahmi (earliest, left-to-right, parent of most Indian scripts), Kharosthi (right-to-left, Gandhara), Gupta → Nagari/Devanagari, Grantha (Sanskrit in the south), Tamil-Brahmi.

**Classical language** status needs antiquity (~1500–2000 yrs), a rich literary heritage and a distinct tradition.

| Language | Year |
|---|---|
| Tamil | 2004 |
| Sanskrit | 2005 |
| Telugu, Kannada | 2008 |
| Malayalam | 2013 |
| Odia | 2014 |
| Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese, Bengali | 2024 |
keyPoints: Four language families: Indo-Aryan (~74%), Dravidian (~25%), Sino-Tibetan, Austric
Tamil = oldest Dravidian language; Telugu = largest Dravidian language
Brahmi is the earliest Indian script (left-to-right); Kharosthi was written right-to-left
Brahmi is the parent script of Gupta → Nagari, Grantha and Tamil-Brahmi
Tamil (2004) was the first classical language; Telugu and Kannada both in 2008
2024 additions: Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese and Bengali

items.title: Streams of Indian Literature — Sangam, Persian and Telugu
items.body:
**Sangam (Tamil):** *Tolkappiyam* (oldest Tamil grammar), the didactic *Tirukkural* (Thiruvalluvar, 1,330 couplets on ethics/polity/love), and the twin epics *Silappadikaram* (Ilango Adigal, theme of Kannagi/justice) and *Manimekalai* (Sathanar, Buddhist). Anthologies: *Ettuthogai* (Eight Anthologies), *Pathupattu* (Ten Idylls).

**Persian & Urdu:** Persian became the court/administrative language from the 12th century. **Amir Khusrau** pioneered Indo-Persian poetry; historical chronicles include Barani's *Tarikh-i-Firuz Shahi*, Abul Fazl's *Akbarnama*, and the royal memoirs *Tuzuk-i-Babari* (Babur, Turkish) and *Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri*. **Urdu** grew from Persian vocabulary over Hindi grammar; **Iqbal** wrote *Bang-i-Dara* and *Saare Jahan Se Achcha*.

**Telugu:** the **Kavitrayam** (Nannaya — *Adi Kavi*, Tikkana, Yerrapragada) rendered the *Andhra Mahabharatam*; Pothana (*Bhagavatam*), Vemana (verse-aphorisms), the potter-poet **Atukuri Molla** (a Telugu *Ramayana*), and Krishnadevaraya's Vijayanagara court (*Amuktamalyada*, and the eight **Ashtadiggajas** led by **Allasani Peddana** — *Andhra Kavita Pitamaha*, author of *Manucharitra*) mark its golden age.
keyPoints: Tolkappiyam is the oldest Tamil grammar; Tirukkural has 1,330 ethical couplets
Silappadikaram and Manimekalai are the twin Tamil epics
Persian was the court language from the 12th century; Amir Khusrau pioneered Indo-Persian poetry
Abul Fazl wrote Akbarnama; Barani wrote Tarikh-i-Firuz Shahi
Iqbal wrote Saare Jahan Se Achcha and Bang-i-Dara (Urdu)
Telugu Kavitrayam = Nannaya, Tikkana, Yerrapragada (Andhra Mahabharatam)
Krishnadevaraya wrote Amuktamalyada; Ashtadiggajas led by Allasani Peddana ('Andhra Kavita Pitamaha', Manucharitra)
Atukuri Molla, a potter-poet, composed a Telugu Ramayana

items.title: Schools of Indian Philosophy (Darshanas)
items.body:
Indian philosophy (*Darshana*, 'intuitive vision') splits on acceptance of Vedic authority.

**Orthodox (Astika) — Shad Darshana:**
| School | Founder | Core idea |
|---|---|---|
| Samkhya | Kapila | Dualism of Purusha & Prakriti (oldest) |
| Yoga | Patanjali | Ashtanga path to liberation |
| Nyaya | Akshapada Gautama | Logic & valid knowledge |
| Vaisheshika | Kanada | Atomism (anu) & elements |
| Mimamsa | Jaimini | Ritual/karma of the Vedas |
| Vedanta | Badarayana (Vyasa) | Brahman as ultimate reality |

Vedanta traditions: **Advaita** (Shankaracharya, non-dualism), **Vishishtadvaita** (Ramanuja, qualified non-dualism), **Dvaita** (Madhvacharya, dualism).

**Heterodox (Nastika)** reject the Vedas: **Buddhism** (Four Noble Truths, Eightfold Path, Anatta), **Jainism** (Ahimsa, Anekantavada, Syadvada), **Charvaka/Lokayata** (Brihaspati, materialism), **Ajivika** (Makkhali Gosala, determinism/Niyati), **Ajnana** (Sanjaya Belatthiputta, skepticism).
keyPoints: Six orthodox schools (Shad Darshana): Samkhya, Yoga, Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Mimamsa, Vedanta
Samkhya (Kapila) is the oldest school — dualism of Purusha and Prakriti
Vedanta traditions: Advaita (Shankara), Vishishtadvaita (Ramanuja), Dvaita (Madhva)
Heterodox schools reject Vedic authority: Buddhism, Jainism, Charvaka, Ajivika, Ajnana
Charvaka (Brihaspati) = materialism; Ajivika (Makkhali Gosala) = determinism (Niyati)
Jain doctrines: Anekantavada (many-sidedness) and Syadvada (conditional predication)

items.title: The Eight Classical Dances
items.body:
All classical dance rests on Bharata Muni's **Natya Shastra**. Basic aspects: **Tandava** (masculine, vigour) and **Lasya** (feminine, grace). Components (Abhinaya Darpana): **Nritta** (pure movement), **Nritya** (expressive), **Natya** (dramatic). Emotion is conveyed by nine *rasas* and 108 *mudras*. The **Sangeet Natak Akademi recognises eight** forms (the Ministry of Culture adds Chhau = nine).

| Dance | State | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Bharatanatyam | Tamil Nadu | Devadasi origin; Carnatic music |
| Kuchipudi | Andhra Pradesh | Dance-drama; Tarangam (plate dance) |
| Kathak | North India | 'Katha'/storytelling; gharanas; Hindustani |
| Kathakali | Kerala | Dance-drama, elaborate make-up, all-male |
| Mohiniyattam | Kerala | Lasya, solo female |
| Odissi | Odisha | 'Mobile sculpture'; Gita Govinda |
| Manipuri | Manipur | Vaishnavite Raslila; soft movements |
| Sattriya | Assam | Sankardev; Vaishnavite monasteries |
keyPoints: Classical dance is based on Bharata Muni's Natya Shastra
Tandava = masculine/vigorous; Lasya = feminine/graceful
Nritta (pure) / Nritya (expressive) / Natya (dramatic); nine rasas, 108 mudras
Sangeet Natak Akademi recognises 8 classical dances; Ministry of Culture adds Chhau (9)
Kerala has two forms: Kathakali (dance-drama) and Mohiniyattam (Lasya)
Sattriya (Assam) was introduced by Srimanta Sankardev; Odissi is called 'mobile sculpture'
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Art & Culture: Classical Dances of India I & II

items.title: Kuchipudi and Indian Classical Music
items.body:
**Kuchipudi (AP):** named after Kuchipudi village; a dance-drama once performed by male-Brahmin *Bhagavathalu*, flourishing under Vijayanagara and Golconda patronage. Shaped into classical form by **Siddhendra Yogi** (*Bhamakalapam*, the story of Satyabhama). Signature **Tarangam** (plate dance — footwork on a brass-plate rim) and **Vachika Abhinaya** (spoken/sung dialogue). Set to Carnatic music; lyrics in Telugu/Sanskrit. Popularised by Vempati Chinna Satyam, Raja & Radha Reddy.

**Music — two systems:**
- **Hindustani** (North): gharanas — Gwalior (oldest), Kirana, Agra, Jaipur, Patiala; exponents like Bhimsen Joshi.
- **Carnatic** (South, incl. AP): elements Sruti, Swara, Raga, Tala; forms Varnam & Kriti. The **Trinity** = Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar, Shyama Shastri. **M.S. Subbulakshmi** was the first musician awarded the Bharat Ratna.
keyPoints: Kuchipudi (AP) shaped by Siddhendra Yogi; signature work Bhamakalapam
Kuchipudi's Tarangam = footwork on the rim of a brass plate; uses Vachika Abhinaya (dialogue)
Two classical music systems: Hindustani (North) and Carnatic (South, incl. AP)
Carnatic Trinity = Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar, Shyama Shastri
Hindustani gharanas include Gwalior, Kirana, Agra, Jaipur, Patiala
M.S. Subbulakshmi was the first musician awarded the Bharat Ratna

items.title: Folk Arts, Crafts and Ancient Science
items.body:
**Folk & craft forms (AP-weighted):**
- Puppetry: **Tholu Bommalata** (AP leather shadow puppets), Kathputli (Rajasthan strings), Bommalattam (Tamil Nadu), Gombeyatta (Karnataka).
- Folk theatre: **Burra Katha** (AP ballad with tambura), Yakshagana (Karnataka), Jatra (Bengal), Tamasha (Maharashtra), Bhavai (Gujarat), Therukoothu (Tamil Nadu).
- Crafts: **Kalamkari** (Srikalahasti/Machilipatnam, AP hand-painted textile), Kondapalli & Etikoppaka wooden toys (AP), Bidri work (Deccan), Phulkari (Punjab).

**Ancient science & mathematics:**
- **Aryabhata** (*Aryabhatiya*, 5th c.): decimal place-value, use of zero, value of π, eclipses via earth's rotation.
- **Varahamihira**: *Brihat Samhita* & *Panchasiddhantika* (astronomy/astrology).
- **Brahmagupta**: rules for zero and negative numbers.
- **Sushruta Samhita**: surgery, including rhinoplasty; **Charaka Samhita**: medicine/Ayurveda.

**Ancient centres of learning:** Takshashila, **Nalanda** (Gupta/Pala patronage), Vikramshila, Valabhi.
keyPoints: Tholu Bommalata (leather shadow puppets) and Burra Katha are Andhra Pradesh folk forms
Kalamkari (Srikalahasti/Machilipatnam) is a hand-painted AP textile craft
Aryabhata: decimal place-value, zero, value of π, earth's rotation explaining eclipses
Varahamihira wrote Brihat Samhita and Panchasiddhantika (astronomy/astrology)
Brahmagupta framed rules for zero and negative numbers
Sushruta Samhita = surgery (incl. rhinoplasty); Charaka Samhita = medicine/Ayurveda
Ancient centres of learning: Takshashila, Nalanda, Vikramshila, Valabhi
